A SMALL FIELD GUIDE

Same keys. Different shapes.

Use the controls to make the rules visible. These are demonstrations, not proofs of expected performance.

01

Read the path

Smaller keys go left; larger keys go right. Every insertion first follows this rule to an empty child.

02

Read the rotation

Orange moves up, rose moves down. The middle subtree changes its parent while keeping the same sorted order.

03

Try an awkward input

Compare increasing, converging, and pairs. A rule that looks good on random keys can struggle with a structured sequence.

Use this viewer with your own implementation

Export a version 1 JSON trace with a sequence and a snapshot after each comparison, insertion, decision, and rotation. The viewer only needs nodes, child links, event explanations, and counters. Import it above to replay it with the same controls. The local Python server runs the repository’s actual strategies; static hosting uses a browser reference simulator with a different seeded random generator.

Treaps store priorities; the experimental metadata-free BSTs do not. Priority labels are scaled to [0, 1) for readability; comparisons use the full 32-bit values.

Reference: Brodal, Bottom-up Rebalancing Binary Search Trees by Flipping a Coin ↗
